C0.quote: voting over two alternatives A and B

C1.quote: multiple stable equilibria in which elections are nearly tied
C1.note: Main results are equilibrium limit characterization and jury theorem.

C2.1.value: vote / action (vote for a candidate or abstain)
C2.1.quote: action of each voter is to vote for one of the two candidates

C2.2.quote: vote for one of the two candidates {A, B}, or abstain
C2.2.note: Input is a vote for one of two alternatives or abstention.

C2.3.quote: Each voter is either a supporter of A (prefers A

C2.4.quote: voting for the less preferred candidate is strictly dominated
C2.4.note: Preferences/types are held attitudes; actions are vote for preferred candidate or abstain.

C3.1.quote: each player picks an action that maximizes her expected utility
C3.1.note: All main analyses are equilibrium analyses with utility-maximizing voters.

C4.1.note: C2.2 = OTH, so the applicability condition for C4.1 is not met.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: Results concern CJT accuracy and winning probability, not welfare or voter-utility criteria.

VOT.quote_behav: each player picks an action that maximizes her expected utility
VOT.quote_info: commonly known joint distribution D over [0, 1] × {A, B}
VOT.note: Voters know own type and common distribution/prior over others' types.

CAN.note: Candidates are only alternatives, not acting agents.

ORG.note: No organizer or election authority acts in the model.

BRI.note: No briber or external manipulator present.

DES.note: No rule/mechanism designer is modelled as an acting agent.

OTH.note: No other acting agent type present.

C7.1.note: Fewer than two types present by the C6 definition; only VOT is present.

C8.1.note: The solution concept is Bayes-Nash equilibrium.

C9.1.note: No abstract/intro/conclusion claims about real institutions, voter well-being, or which rule should be used.

C10.1.note: No explicit procedural reading or statement that inputs are studied only as submitted inputs.
